The difficulty of deploying humanoid robots — one of the key mechanisms by which AI will become pervasive in the real world — remains a problem that many companies are working on using Nvidia’s chips and software.

The problems are so complex and expensive that the field is now only served by well-funded companies, Nvidia said.

To help open up the work to as many as possible, Nvidia is working with Agile Robots SE to create an open robotics platform that researchers can use to do development work. It’ll come with Nvidia’s Jetson Thor computer hardware inside of an Agile One SN humanoid.

In the automotive field, Nvidia said Volvo AB is making self-driving cars that use its chips. Volkswagen AG is using Nvidia products for commercial vehicles, and Bolt Technology OU is using the tech company’s software and gear for robotaxis.

title: Taiwan rejects Grab’s US$600 mil takeover of Foodpanda unit
article:
(Oct 21): Taiwanese authorities blocked Grab Holdings Ltd’s US$600 million ($767 million) takeover of Foodpanda’s local unit, a setback for the ride and food-delivery firm’s expansion plans.

Taiwan’s Fair Trade Commission rejected the deal following an antitrust review, according to a statement Wednesday. The commission said it held talks with the parties on potential merger remedies, but the proposed commitments were insufficient to address competition concerns.

Southeast Asian ride-hailing and delivery leader Grab sought to expand on the island of about 23 million people to find growth beyond its intensely competitive home market. Grab has seen sales slow dramatically as it takes steps to focus on profitability.

Foodpanda’s owner, Delivery Hero SE of Germany, has faced investor pressure for a sale or divestments to streamline the business.

Shares of Delivery Hero fell 0.8% in early Frankfurt trading. Grab advanced about 0.7% in trading before markets opened in New York.

Singapore-based Grab has struck deals to spur revenue growth beyond its core ride-hailing business, which faces intense competition from rivals such as Indonesia’s GoTo Group. It agreed to acquire a majority stake in buy-now-pay-later platform Atome Financial for US$1.49 billion last month, and earlier in the year purchased Stash Financial for an enterprise value of US$425 million.

See also: SpaceX, Tesla boards to study potential US$3.5 tril merger

“We are disappointed by this outcome,” Grab said in a statement. “Grab’s core business across Southeast Asia remains robust. We will continue to focus our capital and resources on executing our growth roadmap and empowering communities across our regional footprint.”

Foodpanda’s Taiwan operations would have added about 13% to Grab’s delivery gross merchandise value and US$60 million to its 2028 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, said Kai Wang, an analyst at Morningstar. Grab has a target of adjusted Ebitda of US$1.7 billion for that year.

“This will only make a minor dent to Grab’s overall operations,” Wang said.

title: Finance leaders spar over AI bubble after warning by Griffin
article:
(Oct 21): Top finance and investing executives pushed back against suggestions of a bubble in artificial intelligence (AI), after billionaire Ken Griffin warned that investors in the industry should be prepared for setbacks.

Deutsche Bank AG chief executive officer Christian Sewing, speaking in an interview at the Berlin Global Dialogue, said he sees no reason to worry about a sharp reversal in asset prices any time soon. BlackRock Inc CEO Larry Fink argued in favour of pushing ahead with the rapid build-out of AI data centres, saying any delays could threaten economic growth and stoke inflation by driving up computing costs.

“Overall, I don’t think that we are living in a bubble which is bursting,” Sewing said on Bloomberg Television on Wednesday. “Do we see the one or the other setback, also with individual companies? That can happen.”

Investor anxiety over the durability of the AI boom surged in recent weeks amid fears that the substantial upfront capital spending the technology needs will take longer than expected to translate into profits and productivity gains. Anthropic PBC, one of the leading AI developers, could spend US$750 billion (RM3.06 trillion) on additional computing power in the coming years, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

Griffin, whose empire includes hedge fund Citadel and market-maker Citadel Securities, warned on Tuesday that investors are “almost certainly” in a bubble as corporations are grappling with how much they want to spend on the technology.

Fink has previously waved off concerns about an AI bubble, pointing instead to supply shortages and saying demand growth has exceeded expectations. He has also warned delays in the technology’s build-out could ultimately limit access.

See also: Lenovo seeking US$2 bil loan to refinance debt at lower cost — Bloomberg

“If we don’t build out these data centres, it is actually more inflationary because the cost of compute is so high right now,” he said on Wednesday. “And the faster we can build out more data centres, the more compute we have, the faster we can bring down the cost.”

Sewing, who has emerged as one of the most influential business leaders in Germany, said the industrial application of AI is “the chance of the century” for his home country, if it gets the regulatory framework right. Deutsche Bank itself uses the technology to increase efficiency but also to improve controls, he said.

“The fear that we are in front of a bubble is not a justified one,” Sewing said. “But what is different from a bubble is ongoing volatility,” he said, pointing to continued geopolitical tensions.

See also: Citigroup fixed-income traders post higher revenue in 3Q as rivals miss

The CEO, who has turned around Germany’s largest lender since taking over eight years ago, is one of a handful of top executives who regularly speak with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, people familiar with the matter have said. Merz hosted the German government’s first investor conference in Berlin this week, a fresh push by the embattled chancellor to revive growth in Europe’s biggest economy.

Rather than AI, Fink and Sewing both pointed to fiscal deficits as a more immediate area of concern, particularly as the AI industry competes with governments for investor money. US Treasury yields have hit multi-decade highs as markets grapple with a nearly US$2 trillion US fiscal deficit.

“We’re at a time now where we’re finally unlocking private capital, and so the competition for capital is as large as I’ve ever seen in my professional career,” Fink said.

In France, months of debate over the budget have pushed the extra yield investors demand to hold French government debt over German bonds into territory associated with the euro-area debt crisis.

“I wouldn’t call it a debt crisis at this point in time, but I think it’s a wake up call in particular for all public financing that budget disciplinary is key,” Sewing said.

title: SpaceX, Tesla boards to study potential US$3.5 tril merger
article:
(Oct 21): Elon Musk openly endorsed the prospect of combining SpaceX with Tesla Inc, in what would be the biggest-ever corporate merger uniting assets from electric cars to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres to rocket and satellite capabilities.

The world’s richest man said on Tuesday the boards of both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to consider the idea of a combination. “There’s a lot of merit to combining the companies,” Musk said on a conference call after SpaceX announced earnings that beat estimates.

Tesla has a market value of about US$1.5 trillion ($1.9 trillion), while SpaceX is valued at US$2 trillion. When asked on the call about the prospects of merging the two companies, Musk initially said he was “tap dancing through a minefield” before going into more detail. He cautioned that getting enough support from Tesla shareholders may be tricky and that neither committee has settled on terms.

“I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies,” Musk said, adding he can’t be part of the discussions because he is a conflicted party.

SpaceX and Tesla shares both extended gains following the comments. SpaceX climbed as much as 11% in pre-market trading on Wednesday, and Tesla rose as much as 3%.

A merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be a blockbuster, creating a conglomerate spanning electric vehicles, energy storage batteries, rockets and satellites. The stated rationale for bringing those disparate interests together lies in their shared ambitions to leverage artificial intelligence for data centres in space, driverless cars and humanoid robots.

See also: Foxconn buys US$727 mil stake in Mitsubishi Electric unit making EV parts

“There’s no question that Musk wants the merger, and he wants to get it done sooner rather than later,” said Gene Munster, the founder of Deepwater Asset Management, which has invested in both companies. “It was a key question on the call, and Elon said it was a good idea about three times. He’s getting people excited about it, and he wants to bump up the enthusiasm.”

Musk made the comments after SpaceX posted US$4.4 billion in net income for the quarter ended in September, far better than analysts’ average projection of US$1.88 billion. Revenue increased 161% from a year ago and also beat expectations.

Revenue from SpaceX’s AI business — now going by super intelligence, or SI — soared to US$7.56 billion in the quarter, more than nine times what the company generated a year ago. SpaceX has become a major compute and infrastructure supplier to Anthropic PBC, Alphabet Inc and others, and in August acquired Cursor, the developer of a popular AI-powered coding tool.

See also: UniCredit gets ECB go-ahead to take control of Commerzbank

Those factors — along with increased adoption of Grok, the large language models developed by Musk’s xAI — contributed to SpaceX’s AI business posting US$431 million of income from operations in the third quarter. A year ago, the business recorded a US$1.7 billion loss.

The SpaceX Starbase industrial complex and rocket launch facility in Starbase, Texas.

“Super Intelligence was the standout growth driver for the quarter,” SpaceX chief financial officer Bret Johnsen said during the call, pointing to increased demand from clients seeking more computing power, as well as Grok enterprise sales.

SpaceX expects total revenue to rise to as much as US$37 billion in the first quarter of next year, Johnsen said. He indicated that the company expects to keep borrowing, saying there are “a number of available pools of debt capital that we are talking to at the moment”.

SpaceX said subscribers to its satellite-internet service Starlink — its biggest income generator — reached 13.6 million by the third quarter, short of the number analysts were expecting. Revenue from the company’s connectivity business still managed to beat expectations, rising 69% from a year ago to US$5.25 billion.

Whereas SpaceX’s AI and connectivity businesses have taken off, revenue from the company’s unit focused on designing, manufacturing and operating launch vehicles and spacecraft rose just 6% to US$1.77 billion in the third quarter.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

On a conference call, Musk said SpaceX expects to catch both the booster and the ship for the 15th test flight of his giant Starship, planned for next month. The vehicle is expected to be fully reusable, a feat no other rocket has achieved. President Gwynne Shotwell later added that the company expects to attempt the first demonstration of on-orbit refuelling with Starship early next year.

On-orbit refuelling will be necessary for Starship to master for SpaceX’s contract to land humans on the moon for Nasa. The company is supposed to have a prototype ready by next year that can dock with Nasa's Orion spacecraft for Artemis III mission, a precursor to a moon landing planned for 2028. Whether that will be ready on time remains uncertain.

Starship is also essential for launching upgraded Starlink satellites that can provide greater capacity and data speeds than the current spacecraft in orbit. Shotwell said she expects the additional capacity from flying what the company refers to as V3 Starship satellites on a much larger vehicle will allow SpaceX to expand across new markets.

“Connecting cars, robots and the adoption of super intelligence will increase communication demands not in percentages, but in many orders of magnitudes,” Shotwell said. “We expect Starlink alone to represent a significant portion of global internet traffic.”

Starlink’s growth was driven by momentum in the aviation industry for in-flight Wi-Fi and Starshield, a militarised version of the service that is more encrypted and secure, Johnsen said.

Starshield has come under renewed scrutiny since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused the White House and Musk of placing restrictions on the technology, which his country’s forces have used for battlefield communications and operations. Both Musk and Trump have denied involvement in the limitations, igniting a firestorm over technology that’s become indispensable to Ukraine’s war against Russia.

When commenting on a potential SpaceX-Tesla combination, Musk said that he suspects “people out there assume” the merger is a certainty. While he said this would be an overstatement, the deal would have the support of Chad Anderson, the chief executive officer of Space Capital, an early SpaceX investor.

“It makes a ton of sense,” Anderson said. “Combined, it would be the only company owning the full physical-AI stack, from chip fabrication to orbital data centres to autonomous devices on the ground. No competitor has an analogue.”

title: Carrefour cuts profit forecast after riots, looting in France
article:
(Oct 21): Carrefour SA warned that the social unrest roiling France will drag on its earnings this year, the first sign of the economic impact from riots in Paris and other cities last weekend.

The grocer cut its profit outlook and other annual financial targets, sending its shares plunging by as much as 15% in Paris trading on Wednesday, the biggest intraday decline since 2017.

“There is a high degree of uncertainty regarding consumer spending trends and the conditions under which our stores will be able to open,” Chief executive officer Alexandre Bompard said late on Tuesday, describing the situation in France as unprecedented.

More evidence of the effect on businesses may emerge when retailer Fnac Darty and luxury groups Hermes International SCA and Kering SA publish sales figures this week.

Cost-of-living protests that drew more than half a million people across France turned violent over the weekend as fast-moving groups targeted hundreds of shops, smashing windows and looting merchandise.

See also: VW’s Scania hastens China e-truck push as drivers abandon diesel

While the turmoil has abated after curfews were imposed, protesters have called for another day of unrest on Saturday.

Carrefour is the first retailer to disclose the financial impact of the riots, and likely one of the most affected because of its city-centre and suburban shops in Paris and other towns.

“Weaker sales from an extended period of reduced store hours would push the profit shortfall into high single digits,” wrote Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Charles Allen.

See also: EU officials propose guardrails for insurance risk transfer boom

About 50 Carrefour stores were hit on the first day of rioting, with many looted and badly damaged, Bompard told analysts. That’s leading to lower footfall, reduced opening hours and increased costs for security and logistics, he said. Carrefour sees a maximum possible impact on profitability of around €200 million.

The ultimate hit to French growth will depend on how long disruption lasts, Charlotte de Montpellier, senior economist for France and Switzerland at ING, said in a note. “If unrest remains brief and concentrated, the macroeconomic impact could be relatively limited, but repeated protests, closures and transport disruption would make lost activity harder to recover.”

Roving bands broke into and looted businesses ranging from high-end boutiques to sporting goods stores and supermarkets.

“As we enter the critical end-of-year period for the retail sector, this situation is having a significant impact on consumer spending — which is already under pressure from rising energy costs,” Bompard said.

title: DayOne said to weigh options for US IPO after data centre rout
article:
(Oct 21): DayOne Data Centers Ltd is weighing options for its US initial public offering (IPO), including a potential delay or size cut, as volatility around data centres increases, according to people familiar with the matter.

While Singapore-based DayOne has been waiting for the right window to launch the IPO, it has also been considering the possibility of pushing back the share sale until the market recovers, the people said. Other options include going ahead with a smaller listing that may raise US$2.5 billion ($3.2 billion) to US$3 billion, roughly half of what it had originally aimed for, the people said.

DayOne, whose backers include Coatue and Hillhouse, is continuing to engage with potential investors and still wants to move forward as soon as the market allows, the people said. The company was initially considering raising as much as US$5 billion from the listing as soon as the fourth quarter, people familiar with the matter said previously. It had been eyeing a valuation of about US$20 billion, the people have said.

“Given the recent market volatility, we think DayOne should downsize its capital raise to a smaller US$2.5 billion-US$3 billion deal, adjusting its underlying valuation to offer a more attractive ‘discount’ to ensure order book stability while keeping its multibillion-dollar construction pipeline funded,” said Stephen Yin, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence.

Deliberations are ongoing and DayOne hasn’t made any final decisions, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The company could still opt to move ahead with the offering in the coming weeks, according to the people. DayOne declined to comment.

While data centres have drawn global investor demand amid a boom in sectors related to artificial intelligence (AI), a more negative sentiment has started to have ripple effects on IPOs. DayOne has been raising billions of dollars in private funding rounds as it seeks capital to build out its pipeline.

See also: Princeton Digital Group seeks US$1.2 bil loan for Malaysian data centre — Bloomberg

Australian data centre company Firmus Grid Ltd pulled its roughly US$5 billion IPO when investors balked at the valuation it sought, while AirTrunk, which also operates data centres, delayed a planned real estate investment trust IPO in Singapore to next year.

South Korean digital infrastructure company Elice Inc plunged 32% in its Seoul trading debut on Tuesday. Coreweave Inc’s shares have more than halved since their May peak, and Nscale Ltd is facing pushback over its target IPO valuation, Bloomberg News has reported. On Wednesday, shares of Australian data centre operator Nextdc Ltd plummeted after it cut earnings guidance.

Investors may prefer to buy into DayOne as it is a traditional data centre operator that generates “highly predictable cash flows” by leasing physical space under long-term contracts, according to Bloomberg Intelligence’s Yin. That contrasts with neoclouds like Firmus and Elice, which carry higher execution risks by renting out access to compute capacity based on graphics processing unit chips, he said. DayOne offers a “vastly superior growth and scale profile”, he said.

See also: DayOne inks RM15 bil multi-currency financing arrangement with seven banks

Some market participants are hoping that the recent volatility will pass after the US midterm elections on Nov 3. They are also looking ahead to the performance of Anthropic PBC’s upcoming listing as an important gauge of sentiment towards the AI sector.

DayOne filed for a US IPO earlier this month. The offering is being led by Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase & Co, Bank of America Corp and Citigroup Inc. IFR reported on Monday that DayOne was gathering more investor feedback before launching the share sale.

DayOne is running or developing data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain. Other backers include GDS Holdings Ltd, the SoftBank Vision Fund and Citadel’s Ken Griffin.

title: Lenovo seeking US$2 bil loan to refinance debt at lower cost — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): Lenovo Group Ltd is seeking a US$2 billion loan priced more cheaply than an earlier facility that it plans to refinance, according to people familiar with the matter, as banks in Asia remain eager to lend to major Chinese firms amid a dearth of deals.

 

The five-year facility, which it has launched into syndication, is priced at 75 basis points (bps) over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR), said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matter.

The pricing is considerably tighter than the 110bps plus a credit adjustment spread over SOFR that Lenovo got for an equal-sized loan in 2022. The adjustment was related to the shift to SOFR from the London Interbank Offered Rate, the people added.

Lenovo is marketing the new loan as its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure business continues to grow. The company’s revenue jumped 43% in the quarter ended June and it has boosted its fiscal year outlook. It also comes in the midst of a deal drought in the broader Asia loan market, especially from Chinese borrowers who are able to tap cheaper funding onshore.

There have been only 54 offshore Chinese loan deals completed so far this year, a 17-year low, down from a peak of 135 borrowings in the same period in 2019, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. The value of deals, however, has jumped to about US$56.1 billion from US$38.4 billion a year ago, due mainly to TikTok developer ByteDance’s US$29.6 billion loan last month, Bloomberg-compiled data showed.

ByteDance’s three-year loan, which is one of the largest dollar-denominated borrowings in Asia this year, had an opening margin of 68bps over SOFR, compared with a previous offshore facility it secured with an 85 basis point margin. Smartphone maker Oppo, meanwhile, is raising a US$1.2 billion-equivalent three-year loan offering a margin of only 50bps over SOFR.

BNP Paribas, Citigroup Inc, DBS Bank Ltd, HSBC Holdings plc and JPMorgan Chase Bank, NA Hong Kong are the coordinators of the Lenovo loan.

See also: Citigroup fixed-income traders post higher revenue in 3Q as rivals miss

Lenovo’s shares have slumped about 25% this month as concerns rise over the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure projects, but they are still up around 125% over the past year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Lenovo separately raised US$2 billion from a seven-year convertible bonds sale in June and plans to use the proceeds to refinance existing debt and fund share buybacks.

title: HDFC Bank probe finds that senior executives leaked secrets — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): An internal probe by HDFC Bank Ltd — India’s largest by market value — found evidence that two senior executives disclosed confidential business strategies and possible market-sensitive information to outsiders, according to people familiar with the matter.

The executives oversee certain key businesses and functions at the bank, according to the people, who asked not to be named discussing confidential matters.

HDFC identified the executives during an internal investigation that began after some leaders grew concerned about the possibility of information being leaked, the people said. The probe is still underway as the bank continues to examine whether the information was misused, the people said.

An HDFC Bank spokesperson acknowledged an internal review, but didn’t comment on its findings or the executives involved. “In line with our policies, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts,” the spokesperson said by email. “Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, once the review is complete.”

The bank said it was committed to upholding the highest standards of ethics and governance and takes reports of potential violations seriously.

The review comes at a sensitive moment for HDFC Bank, which has a market value of about US$115 billion ($147 billion) and has spent three decades cultivating a reputation for conservative management, strong internal controls and consistent profitability. The lender is preparing for its first outsider chief executive following boardroom disputes and management departures. Its share price has declined about 28% this year.

See also: BHP cuts 300 workers at Australian iron ore mines as costs rise

The probe and its findings were reported to senior management, including some members of the board, earlier this year, the people said. Both executives have since been formally informed of the findings, and it wasn’t immediately clear what disciplinary action will be taken, the people said.

The findings add to the challenges confronting Anup Bagchi, a veteran of rival ICICI Group, who is set to become HDFC Bank’s chief executive on Oct 27.

In recent months, internal divisions in HDFC have played out publicly. In March, then-chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned abruptly, citing differences between his personal values and certain practices at the bank. An independent legal review commissioned by the lender subsequently said his concerns were not substantiated.

See also: HSBC moves to Wall Street bonus model as it cuts fixed-pay deals

Bagchi’s appointment follows the surprise decision of Sashidhar Jagdishan, the incumbent chief executive, not to seek another term. Jagdishan is stepping down after six years at the helm.

Kaizad Bharucha, deputy managing director and one of the bank’s longest-serving executives, has also asked to leave at the end of December.

Founded in 1994, as the country opened its financial sector to private competition, HDFC Bank grew into a preferred investment for international fund managers seeking exposure to India’s rising incomes and expanding consumer credit.

title: Nickel rallies past US$16,000 on prospect of Indonesia output cuts
article:
(Oct 21): Nickel rose for a fourth day as the prospect of coordinated output cuts by Chinese producers in Indonesia raised expectations of tighter supply.

The metal climbed as much as 2.7% to exceed US$16,000 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME), building on gains since hitting a nine-month low last Thursday.

Executives from several major Chinese nickel producers are considering potential output curbs at their Indonesian operations, including plants that produce a key feedstock for batteries. A previous attempt to agree on cuts in August was unsuccessful.

“What everyone is really focused on right now is the size of the production cuts,” said Gao Yin, an analyst at Shuohe Asset Management Co. “The numbers being circulated in the market are quite significant.”

Producers in Indonesia have been grappling with weaker prices and rising costs, while tighter mining quotas have also constrained ore supplies. The Southeast Asian nation dominates global nickel production, making changes to output there a key driver for the market.

Elsewhere, the Middle East’s biggest aluminium producer Emirates Global Aluminium said it has restored half the capacity at its main smelter that was hit during the Iran war. It maintained its target of returning to full capability by the first quarter of next year.

See also: Copper mines need US$332 bil new investment to ease shortfall

The aluminium market has been roiled this year by the Iran war, disrupting flows of metal from the Middle East — which accounts for about 10% of global production — sending prices and premiums higher.

Aluminium was 0.8% higher on the LME at 9.59am local time. Nickel was up 2.1% at US$16,005 a tonne, trimming this year’s decline to less than 4%. Other metals were little changed.

title: Musk says ASML, others expediting chipmaking gear for Terafab
article:
(Oct 21): ASML Holding NV and other key providers of chipmaking machines have expedited supplies for Tesla Inc and SpaceX’s Terafab, Elon Musk said, signalling that the billionaire is making fast progress on an ambitious semiconductor project.

SpaceX is targeting volume chip production at its Terafab facility by the third or fourth quarter of 2028, Musk said.

“These are very aggressive dates, and we are very appreciative of ASML and all of our other suppliers in accelerating equipment deliveries in order to achieve this outcome,” Musk, the chief executive officer of Tesla and SpaceX, said during the latter company’s third-quarter earnings call.

Terafab is Musk’s plan for handling the mass-scale chip manufacturing needed by SpaceX and Tesla. The goal of the project is to make up for a shortfall in cutting-edge artificial intelligence processors and other chips from current suppliers such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC).

An ASML spokesperson declined to comment. The Veldhoven, Netherlands-based company’s shares rose 2.1% in early Amsterdam trading on Wednesday.

title: Carlsberg close to filing IPO for Indian unit for US$700 mil — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): Carlsberg A/S is preparing to publicly file documents for an initial public offering (IPO) of its India business, which could raise as much as US$700 million (RM2.86 billion), as early as this week, according to people familiar with the matter.

 

Carlsberg India, the country’s second-largest brewer, is expected to begin investor roadshows next week and could launch the IPO as early as December, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The proposed IPO is expected to consist entirely of a secondary share sale by the Danish brewer, the people said. Carlsberg confidentially submitted draft IPO documents in July.

Carlsberg is working with Kotak Mahindra Capital Co, as well as the Indian units of JPMorgan Chase & Co and Citigroup Inc, on the proposed offering, people familiar with the matter have said.

Deliberations are ongoing and details including the size, structure and timing of the transaction could change, the people said. A representative for Carlsberg didn’t respond immediately to a request for comment.

India’s IPO market has regained momentum after a subdued first half of 2026. Companies have raised about US$14.4 billion through first-time share sales so far this year, putting the market on course for another strong year after a record US$22 billion was raised in 2025. Jio Platforms Ltd’s record US$3.2 billion offering was fully subscribed within hours of opening for bids on Wednesday.

Carlsberg India has a market share of about 22%. The company, which entered India in 2007, operates seven breweries across the country, according to its website.

title: Starbucks China will require purchases to sit in its cafes
article:
(Oct 21): Starbucks Corp will require customers to make a purchase to sit in its China cafes, part of a push to revive its fortunes in the competitive mainland market.

The new seating policy will take effect nationwide from Oct 22, with stores displaying notices informing customers of the change, Starbucks China said on Wednesday.

“We will continue investing resources to improve the in-store experience, and work together with customers to create and maintain a welcoming third-place experience,” the company said in a statement.

Starbucks China also plans additional investment in fiscal 2027, including adding staff during peak hours, upgrading digital systems and core equipment, and renovating about 1,000 mainland outlets, according to a separate statement on WeChat.

The changes come as Starbucks tries to make its cafes more appealing while battling intensifying competition in China. The chain agreed last November to sell a majority stake in its China business to private equity firm Boyu Capital at a US$4 billion enterprise value, bringing in a local partner to help chart its next phase of growth.

Starbucks China posted comparable-store sales declines in each of the past two fiscal years, weighed down by fierce competition and price wars. Sales showed signs of recovery earlier this fiscal year, though the business has yet to demonstrate a sustained return to growth as it transitions to its new ownership structure. Starbucks stopped separately disclosing China’s performance from the third quarter ended in June.

See also: India steps up overseas investment checks as rupee slides

The seating change echoes last year’s move by Starbucks in the US, where the company reversed a policy allowing anyone — even those who hadn’t purchased food or drinks — to use its cafes, patios and restrooms. Starbucks said the change was intended to prioritise paying customers and introduced a new code of conduct as part of chief executive officer Brian Niccol’s effort to make its stores more appealing.

Starbucks has about 8,000 stores in China after first opening in Beijing in 1999. But its position has come under pressure in recent years as cheaper local rivals including Luckin Coffee Inc have expanded rapidly and consumers have become more reluctant to pay a premium for foreign brands.

Luckin dethroned Starbucks as China’s biggest coffee chain three years ago, helped by drinks that cost a fraction of the price. Starbucks’ bigger, more expensive store format has also come under pressure as customers grow increasingly cautious about discretionary spending amid China’s economic slowdown.

title: Lane says greater global euro use may help ECB control inflation
article:
(Oct 21): Wider global usage of the euro could help the European Central Bank hit its inflation target, according to chief economist Philip Lane.

Greater use of the euro internationally “supports the ability of the ECB to achieve price stability by increasing the international impact of euro-area monetary policy and thereby influencing foreign demand, as well as domestic demand,” Lane said Wednesday in a speech in Shanghai.

In addition, a stronger international role for the common currency would reduce the sensitivity of the bloc’s import prices to external shocks by fostering invoicing in euro, he said.

ECB officials have repeatedly advocated an expanded global footprint for the euro to bolster European sovereignty in the face of dwindling support from the US, as well as increase trade and lower borrowing costs.

Should the currency’s international status be boosted, Lane said higher ECB interest rates would weaken foreign demand and, in turn, bolster inflation-fighting efforts.

“A tightening of euro-area monetary policy makes it more expensive for foreign entities to source euro denominated funding, which weighs on demand in economies that use the euro, particularly for debt issuance, as well as for trade invoicing and funding of working capital,” he said.

See also: US-Mexico trade talks hit impasse as Lutnick exerts influence — Bloomberg

To increase the euro’s appeal, the ECB has already begun offering euro liquidity to most central banks around the world.

“The monetary-policy case for liquidity lines is reinforced by their dynamic interaction with other policy areas,” Lane said.

title: Getty files for bankruptcy in process that will take it private
article:
(Oct 21): Getty Images Holdings Inc is starting a prepackaged bankruptcy after securing a restructuring support agreement that will inject it with fresh money and take the photo archive and stock-image company private.

The company filed for Chapter 11 proceedings in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. Getty listed assets of US$1 billion (RM4.08 billion) to US$10 billion, and liabilities in the same range.

The company has moved forward to implement its previously disclosed financial restructuring, it said. The step includes an equity investment of up to US$533 million from parties including members of the Getty family and affiliates of Koch Equity Development. The company had previously disclosed those parties would provide new equity.

The filling followed prolonged negotiations as the company wrestled with a high debt load and a shift of customers using AI-generated images instead of stock photos. Getty entered into a 30-day grace period after failing to make interest payments due Sept 1 on unsecured notes. At the time, the company said it had cash to make the payments but elected to use the reprieve to iron out a consensual workout deal.

Suppliers will be paid in full under the restructuring plan.

title: Ex-official expects Japan's central bank to hike rates every quarter
article:
(Oct 21): The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will probably keep raising interest rates every three months to contain risks of inflation deviating from its stable price target, according to a former BOJ executive director who oversaw monetary policy.

“I expect the next rate hike in December, followed by another in March or April,” Eiji Maeda said in an interview on Tuesday. “The pace has now accelerated to roughly one hike every three months, and I think that’s appropriate.”

It is also broadly in line with market pricing. The overnight swaps market implies investors see a roughly 80% chance of an increase by December. The BOJ is widely expected to hold rates steady at its next policy meeting on Oct 30.

The bank’s hikes last month and in June amounted to its fastest pace since 1990. They were delivered against a backdrop of accelerating consumer prices, and yen weakness that triggered a joint intervention by Tokyo and Washington, and US pressure for tighter monetary policy.

Maeda, who led the BOJ’s initial response to the Covid pandemic, doesn’t completely rule out the idea that the bank may in future opt to hike in successive meetings, in circumstances such as a sharp depreciation of the yen. But he said it doesn’t seem likely at this point.

“If the BOJ delivers back-to-back hikes, markets may increasingly expect another consecutive move, and that carries significant risk,” Maeda said. “That gives the BOJ reason to avoid hiking at consecutive meetings.”

A key focus of the October meeting is whether governor Kazuo Ueda’s board will judge that underlying inflation has hit its 2% target for the first time since the goal was set in 2013.

“I don’t expect the BOJ to go so far as to clearly say that the 2% price stability target has been achieved,” Maeda said. “But it wouldn’t be surprising if it moved its assessment forward somewhat.”

Data due out Friday is expected to show headline inflation climbed to 2.1% in September, while a core rate that strips out fresh food and energy accelerated to 2.3%.

See also: BOJ to lean against back-to-back rate hike in October — Bloomberg

Ueda said last week that the bank can no longer tolerate a rise in underlying inflation because it’s very close to the target, an indication of his backing for further rate hikes.

Japan is emerging from a long period of deflationary pressures. While underlying inflation can now finally be assessed as being around 2%, the bank’s mission isn’t accomplished, as the goal is to make inflation stabilise around that level, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg.

Still, it would be a signal for a December hike if the bank judges the price trend is around its goal while financial conditions remain accommodative next week, said Maeda, who is now president of the Chibagin Research Institute.

The September rate increase brought the BOJ’s policy rate to 1.25%, entering its estimated range of a neutral rate between 1.1% and 2.5% for the first time. The neutral rate is the level that is neither stimulative nor restrictive to the economy. Maeda said the BOJ may eventually be forced to lift its benchmark rate to 2.25%, which would essentially mean four more hikes.

“If the midpoint of around 1.75% is taken as one benchmark, the policy rate would reach neutral around next spring,” said Maeda, who was also the chief economist of the BOJ. From around that time on, “policy decisions — and explaining them — may become more difficult.”

title: Boeing wins US approval for largest variant of 737 Max jet
article:
(Oct 21): Boeing Co won US regulator approval for its 737 Max 10 jet, capping off a lengthy certification saga for the plane-maker’s family of narrowbody aircraft that was disrupted by two fatal crashes and a series of quality lapses.

The 737 Max 10 is the largest of the company’s single-aisle aircraft and is Boeing’s response to rival Airbus SE’s A321neo. The plane’s 1,500-plus order book makes it one of the more popular Max variants, purchased by US carriers like United Airlines Holdings Inc and Alaska Air Group Inc. The Max 10’s smallest sibling, the 737 Max 7, was approved by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in August.

“The FAA’s decision follows a thorough review of the aircraft’s design and safety requirements,” FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said in a news release, adding that the regulator will “continue to hold Boeing to the highest safety standards” moving forward.

Bloomberg reported in July that the FAA was expected to certify the Max 10 around October. The timeline was briefly in doubt after the plane-maker disclosed a software glitch with the airplane’s navigation system, but an FAA panel determined the issue did not pose a safety risk.

“The 737-10 offers greater capacity, longer range and the best seat economics in its class, a platform that will create more value and opportunities for airlines around the world,” Boeing Commercial Airplanes chief executive officer Stephanie Pope said in a statement on Tuesday.

The Max 10 is one of Boeing’s most important new jets, offering airlines a solution to replace the out-of-production 757. Alongside the other Max models, the largest variant will help the plane-maker repair its balance sheet and pare down debt. The aircraft can seat as many as 230 passengers and fly for up to 3,100 nautical miles, according to Boeing’s website.

See also: GE lifts outlook as air travel boom shrugs off fuel costs

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said streamlining aircraft certification is essential to America’s ability to compete with Europe and China, noting that it took nearly a decade to approve the Max 10. “I have to allow you all to certify ​aircraft faster,” Duffy told a ceremony at Boeing’s widebody site north of Seattle on Tuesday. “You have to come to the market more quickly.”

Regulators in Canada and Europe are expected to complete their own Max 10 approvals in “probably a couple months”, Mike Sinnett, a Boeing executive over development programmes, said later.

title: Morgan Stanley sees fuel tightness persisting through mid-2027
article:
(Oct 21): Oil-product markets are likely to remain tight through mid-2027, even if current war-related disruptions ease, as an “unusually large upswing in refinery maintenance” constrains global supply, according to Morgan Stanley.

Planned outages at the world’s refineries through the second quarter of next year are set to rise by 3.4 million barrels a day, analysts including Martijn Rats and Charlotte Firkins said in a note published Tuesday. That’s two and a half times the norm, and greater than the current refinery-run cuts in the Middle East and Russia, they said.

Global markets are contending with a fuel crunch following nearly eight months of war in the Middle East, as well as a recent surge in attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other’s energy infrastructure. For fuels like diesel — vital to transport, heating and industry — a sharp drop in exports has led to more severe price spikes than for crude.

Refineries have postponed maintenance to take advantage of strong margins. But work “cannot be delayed indefinitely,” the analysts wrote. The second quarter of 2007 “already looked like a quarter with a lot of maintenance outages, but this has grown further over time,” they added. Furthermore, there’s likely to be “little recovery in refinery runs” by then.

title: AI to spur Southeast Asian digital economy to US$368 bil, study shows
article:
(Oct 21): Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping Southeast Asia’s digital economy deliver robust growth in the face of rising prices and teetering demand, according to a group of researchers.

Online spending across the region will rise about 17% this year to US$368 billion ($470 billion), a report from Google, Temasek Holdings Pte Ltd and Bain & Co showed, a slight slowdown from a year earlier. While sputtering economic growth and elevated inflation are weighing on consumer demand in categories from e-commerce to travel, the region’s digital businesses have harnessed AI to better target consumers and spur spending.

The region of about 700 million people is a battleground for e-commerce giants such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd and Shopee parent Sea Ltd, ride-hailing and food-delivery firms including Grab Holdings Ltd and GoTo Group, and online travel agencies like Trip.com Group Ltd and Traveloka. To cope with the intense competition, the companies are betting on rising internet use and consumer spending to fuel their revenue growth.

Still, elevated inflation and interest rates, as well as jolts to energy prices from geopolitical shocks, are weighing on consumers’ spending power. Concerns that any retreat in the world’s AI push could reduce demand at Southeast Asia’s crucial hardware industry are further tapering expectations for the regional economy.

AI is helping digital businesses partially offset such risks. Online media is on track to grow at its strongest pace in at least five years, helped by swelling advertising revenue from AI promoting content, according to the report. About 62% of Southeast Asian consumers are now more confident using AI to make critical decisions than they were last year, the report showed.

See also: Anthropic may spend US$750 bil in coming years, report says

AI is also fuelling the region’s tech investment rebound. Funding for the region’s private companies surged more than fivefold in the first half of this year compared with the same period last year, according to the report. Major deals to construct data centers spurred investments, along with demand to apply AI in industries from software to digital financial services.

Many of the deals concentrated on companies that stand to gain from the global AI boom, such as data centre operators. Among them, firms including STT GDC and DayOne Data Centers Ltd accounted for a bulk of the funding.

title: Anthropic may spend US$750 bil in coming years, report says
article:
(Oct 21): Anthropic PBC could spend US$750 billion ($959 billion) on additional computing power in the coming years, according to a Wall Street Journal (WSJ) report, as the company prepares for an initial public offering (IPO).

The AI firm had a net loss of US$80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, the media outlet reported, citing a draft IPO prospectus. That compares to a net loss of US$13 billion in the corresponding period a year ago, the WSJ said.

The overwhelming majority of the net loss in the first half of this year, US$72 billion, resulted from accounting charges linked to changes in the value of convertible notes and other instruments Anthropic has issued, according to the report.

Anthropic, one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) developers, is expected to publicly file paperwork for a Wall Street debut in the coming weeks, setting it up for what could be one of the largest IPOs ever. The listing will help the company raise additional capital to support its investments in chips, data centres and talent to build new and better AI models.

The company behind Claude spent close to US$9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the six months ended June 30, versus US$2.3 billion in the same period in 2025, according to the WSJ. Anthropic deployed more funds to secure computing power in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025, when it spent US$7.3 billion.

The prospectus showed Anthropic’s extensive web of computing power agreements — totalling around US$450 billion in the next seven to 10 years — the majority of which can’t be cancelled, according to the WSJ. The company plans to spend US$111 billion on contracts with Alphabet Inc’s Google Cloud, US$110 billion with Amazon.com Inc’s Amazon Web Services and US$31 billion with Microsoft Corp.

See also: AI fears return with data centre firm Elice’s 33% debut flop in Seoul

Anthropic’s prospectus flags the risk of damages caused by AI, including the potential for models to show “self-preserving” qualities to avoid being turned off, and responses that resemble “blackmail” to keep humans from preventing them from operating, the report showed. Anthropic could also face the risk of political resistance to building data centres in the US, where most of its capacity is, according to the WSJ.

The company told investors it had achieved profitability in the third quarter on an adjusted basis, Bloomberg News has reported. Anthropic is generating positive free cash flow, had a gross margin of 85% and an over 11% positive adjusted operating margin as of the third quarter, people familiar with the matter have said.

The company is set to begin formally marketing its IPO as soon as the week of Nov 9, putting it in line to begin trading before the US Thanksgiving holiday, Bloomberg News has reported. It is expected to make its debut no later than the end of the year.

title: US-Mexico trade talks hit impasse as Lutnick exerts influence — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): US and Mexican trade negotiators have hit an impasse over tariffs on steel and aluminum, dashing earlier optimism for an imminent deal and likely kicking major progress until after the midterm elections, people familiar with the matter said.

Talks have cooled off in recent days after US officials including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick took issue with Mexican officials’ demands for reduced tariffs on metals, according to two of the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private deliberations.

Lutnick has sought to exert more influence in the talks and broader trade policy after taking a back seat to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, whose office earlier spearheaded the negotiations, according to the people. Lutnick met virtually with Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum on Sept 9.

The White House and Commerce Departments did not respond to requests for comment.

Mexican officials had earlier expressed hope that a deal was within the negotiators’ grasp. One sticking point is around lowering tariffs on derivative metals products. Duties on downstream products made from steel and aluminum have amassed to cover a substantial part of Mexico’s economy, and Mexican leaders have said they did not want a deal without relief on that.

Talks between the two countries stalled after a counter-proposal from Lutnick failed to address Mexican concerns, the people said. Now, US officials have grown comfortable with the idea of kicking a potential deal down the road, well after the Nov 3 midterm elections.

See also: Brazil moves to contain bird virus, suspends chicken exports to Malaysia

“We’re a little bit stuck on the details,” Roberto Lazzeri, Mexico’s ambassador to the US and one of several officials who have participated in US trade negotiations, said Monday on a panel in Miami. The Wall Street Journal first reported the impasse in talks.

“I think the sticking point is the 232 tariffs,” Lazzeri said, referring to the duties imposed by the Trump administration under Section 232 of the Trade Act of 1974, which include a 50% import tax on steel and aluminum, and a 25% import tax on for non-US content on USMCA-compliant cars.

Mexico’s Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard, who is Mexico’s lead negotiator, rejected the suggestion that Lutnick was blocking a potential deal.

See also: Japan’s export growth stays solid, supported by chips, cars

“In my last conversation with him, I didn’t get the impression that he was opposed to reducing those tariffs, at least as far as I know,” Ebrard told reporters late last week.

A framework agreement between the US and Mexico would provide stability and certainty to business leaders who are stalling investment decisions amid rolling negotiations over renewing the US-Mexico-Canada trade deal. Another point of contention has been industry-specific tariff rates, which Mexican officials have argued give other countries, including Japan and Korea, an upper hand.

Mexico’s economy is heavily dependent on trade with the US, with more than 80% of its exports going to its northern neighboru. The government has sought a deal that would see US tariffs on light vehicles go to 15% from the current 25%, according to other officials, who also asked not to be identified. The proposed agreement also included a reduction in the 50% tariffs on steel and aluminum, although the two sides had not settled on a new rate.

The disagreements echo those that caused the breakdown of US and Canada talks in August, which was largely driven by Lutnick’s opposition to proposed concessions on industry specific, Section 232 tariffs — which fall under the Commerce Department’s jurisdiction.

On Tuesday, Sheinbaum struck a positive note about reaching “the best possible” trade deal.

“We haven’t reached a final agreement yet, but we’ve come quite a long way,” she said at a daily press briefing.

title: Brazil moves to contain bird virus, suspends chicken exports to Malaysia
article:
SAO PAULO (Oct 21): Brazil raced to contain the trade fallout from the detection of a highly contagious bird virus, as poultry shipments to countries including top buyer China faced restrictions.

Brazil said Monday that Newcastle disease was identified at a commercial turkey unit in the state of Santa Catarina. The discovery prompted a restriction in trade with several partners, raising the risk of disruptions from the world’s largest poultry exporter that is also home to meatpacking giants including JBS NV and MBRF Global Foods SA.

So far, however, the impact has been fairly limited. Brazil briefly suspended all poultry shipments to China before negotiations resulted in restrictions covering only Santa Catarina. In other major markets including Saudi Arabia, South Korea and the UK, even narrower limits were imposed, around the affected area.

In a previous outbreak of the disease in 2024, Brazil had to halt shipments to China and the European Union. On that occasion, it took 18 months before trade with China was fully restored, with authorities clearing shipments from the state where the virus was detected.

“Unless we see a widespread event happening — which is unusual for this disease and Brazil’s Ministry acted fast to contain spread — we think the impact could be even smaller” amid the limited restrictions, JPMorgan analysts led by Lucas Ferreira wrote in a note.

Newcastle disease attacks the respiratory, nervous and digestive systems of birds. While there’s no evidence that the virus could be transmitted to humans by food, it is typical that importing countries set protocols for shipments, partly as a way of protecting their own producers. 

The virus was found in a turkey that did not present any symptoms, according to Brazil’s Animal Protein Association, or ABPA. To prevent the virus spread to the flock, authorities ordered the culling of all 6,000 animals in the affected production facility.

See also: Japan’s export growth stays solid, supported by chips, cars

Santa Catarina is Brazil’s second-largest supplier of chicken, accounting for roughly 23% of all exports this year through September. Meatpacking companies with plants there may seek to use other plants outside the state to continue serving countries that imposed restrictions.

“The market is seeing very strong demand, and exports will grow this year,” said Ricardo Santin, president of ABPA.

In China’s case, an agreement between the two nations required Brazil to “self-embargo,” although authorities from the Asian nation have the ability to lift or ease restrictions, Santin said.

See also: Maersk and Hateco plan US$3.5 bil Vietnam rail freight project

The situation differs from market to market. Brazil halted all poultry shipments to Malaysia, while Mexico also suspended imports of Brazilian poultry. On a more limited basis, Brazil has restricted shipments from Santa Catarina state to Kazakhstan and Chile, in accordance with sanitary agreements with those countries.

Restrictions are even narrower for some other destinations, with bans limited to processing plants located near the area where the virus was detected. Those measures apply to countries including Argentina, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, the UK and South Korea.

title: Japan’s export growth stays solid, supported by chips, cars
article:
(Oct 21): Japan’s export growth remained solid in September, with shipments of chips and cars rising.

The value of exports rose 16.7% from a year earlier, the Finance Ministry reported Wednesday. That missed economists’ median forecast of a 21.3% increase. Exports have risen for 13 straight months.

Imports rose 18.9%, compared with economists’ estimate of a 20.4% advance. The trade balance was an unadjusted ¥536 billion (US$3.4 billion) deficit, compared with a ¥1.1 trillion deficit in August.

The gain in exports highlighted ongoing demand related to artificial intelligence. Shipments of semiconductors and chip-making equipment surged 49.4% and 43.9%, respectively. Car exports gained 15.1%.

By destination, shipments to the US gained 22.9%. Those to China and the European Union advanced 8.6% and 10.5%, respectively.

Imports of crude oil gained 51.1% by value, compared with a 3.1% increase in volume, as oil prices remained elevated due to tensions in the Middle East.

See also: Maersk and Hateco plan US$3.5 bil Vietnam rail freight project

“Demand for AI-related products remains strong, with semiconductor exports rising, and I expect this trend to continue without any oversupply for the foreseeable future,” said Takeshi Minami, chief economist at the Norinchukin Research Institute. “The situation in the Middle East is spiraling out of control, so high oil prices are likely to persist for some time.”

Japan has been reducing its dependence on oil from the region by cultivating alternative sources. Japan’s crude oil imports from the US jumped 820% by value in September, while shipments from the Middle East gained 1.5% by value. In volume terms, oil imports from the region fell 30%.

Japan’s trade surplus with the US was ¥393 billion. The Trump administration has imposed higher tariffs on Japanese goods in an effort to narrow the US trade deficit with Japan. The two nations struck a trade deal last year that capped tariffs at 15% on most Japanese products in exchange for Tokyo’s pledge to increase investment in the US.

See also: US homebuilder sentiment drops to 14-year low on depressed sales

The yen traded at 157.43 against the dollar on average in September, 6.7% weaker than a year earlier, according to the ministry. A weaker yen makes it more expensive to import materials while it gives exporters a competitive advantage overseas.

title: US stock futures advance on AI earnings boost
article:
(Oct 21) : Asian stocks were set to track US stock futures higher as strong earnings from some of the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom helped revive the tech trade.

Futures for the Nasdaq 100 jumped 1% after SpaceX reported quarterly net income that more than doubled estimates, sending its shares up more than 5% in late trading. Contracts for the S&P 500 rose 0.5% after the underlying benchmark advanced 0.3% on Tuesday. Equity-index futures for Australia, Japan and South Korea all pointed to gains.

Super Micro Computer Inc. also topped expectations, lifting AI-infrastructure shares in extended trading. The company has benefited from surging spending on equipment used to train and run AI models. Meanwhile, Netflix Inc. sank after issuing a disappointing forecast.

Elsewhere, Brent crude settled near US$109. Talks aimed at reaching a deal between the US and Iran are continuing, according to a diplomat involved in the negotiations, who pushed back against reports that an agreement was close. Long-term Treasuries outperformed, weighing on the dollar.

The results offered some reassurance after concerns over AI valuations and financing rattled technology shares last week. Investors now turn to a packed earnings slate for signs that growth can justify the billions being poured into computing infrastructure, with Meta Platforms Inc. due to report Wednesday.

“There are no signs that demand for AI is slowing,” said Angelo Kourkafas at Edward Jones. “We’re seeing healthy skepticism and a maturation of the theme, moving away from an environment where everything AI-related goes up toward a greater focus on quality and the companies with the deepest pockets to finance the investment needed to meet demand.”

See also: Oil steadies as traders weigh conflicting signals on Iran talks

Elon Musk’s satellite, rocket and AI conglomerate posted US$4.4 billion in net income for the quarter ended September, compared with analysts’ average estimate of US$1.88 billion. Revenue surged 161% from a year earlier and also beat expectations.

Separately, Musk said SpaceX and Tesla Inc. have formed special committees to explore a potential merger, a preliminary step toward what would rank as the largest corporate tie-up of all time.

Long-term Treasuries advanced Tuesday as oil retreated from recent highs, easing inflation concerns. Yields from 10 to 30 years fell three to four basis points, with the benchmark 10-year rate declining to 5.11%.

See also: Stocks climb in late hours after SpaceX’s earnings

While oil prices have been a dominant driver of Treasury yields for much of this year, bond investors largely ignored them last week amid a selloff in stocks that have benefited from investment in artificial intelligence.

“The AI risk-off trade that bubbled up last week is still top of mind in rates markets and seems to be driving the price action today, although the move lower in oil also helped put some downward pressure on yields,” said Izaac Brook, US rates strategist at RBC Capital Markets.

title: Oil steadies as traders weigh conflicting signals on Iran talks
article:
(Oct 21): Oil steadied after a choppy session on Tuesday that saw traders parse conflicting headlines on efforts to end the US-Iran war.

West Texas Intermediate traded near US$98 a barrel, while Brent closed below US$109 on Tuesday after trading in a range of more than $6. While talks aimed at ending the conflict are continuing, reports that an agreement is close are inaccurate, according to a diplomat involved in negotiations.

An earlier unconfirmed report on Iran war negotiations had knocked oil off five-month highs, with Brent at one point falling as much as 3.3% before paring losses. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said he has to make a final decision about which way he wants to win, referring to the conflict.

Brent has surged almost 80% this year as widening conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine disrupt energy supplies, with refined products climbing even more sharply. Renewed attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure are keeping geopolitical risk elevated even as Persian Gulf flows recover to near pre-war levels.

“This conflict doesn’t feel like it’s coming to a quick conclusion,” said Dan Pickering, chief investment officer at Pickering Energy Partners. Traders “are settling in for a higher-priced environment while respecting the volatility in the near-end of the curve.”

Separately, the industry-funded American Petroleum Institute reported US crude inventories fell by 4.9 million barrels last week, according to a document seen by Bloomberg. If confirmed by official data on Wednesday, it would mark a third weekly decline.

title: Stocks climb in late hours after SpaceX’s earnings
article:
(Oct 21) : Stocks rose in late hours as SpaceX reported solid earnings fueled by a big jump in its artificial-intelligence business.

An exchange-traded fund tracking the S&P 500 gained after the close of regular trading. Elon Musk’s satellite, rocket and AI conglomerate posted US$4.4 billion in net income for the quarter ended in September, topping the average projection of US$1.88 billion. Super Micro Computer Inc.’s preliminary results beat estimates. Netflix Inc. sank on a disappointing forecast.

In regular hours, more than 400 firms in the US equity benchmark rose. Brent oil settled near US$109. Despite inaccurate reports that a peace agreement between the US and Iran is close, talks aimed at reaching a deal continue, according to a diplomat involved in negotiations. Long-term Treasuries outperformed.

Investors around the world will be closely watching a spate of tech earnings for clues on whether the AI boom can justify the billions of dollars being poured into the industry. Following SpaceX’s results, attention will soon shift to Meta Platforms Inc.’s figures on Wednesday.

The key question is whether recent growth rates can be sustained as comparisons become more demanding and macroeconomic risks persist, according to Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Chief Investment Office.

“We expect a strong third-quarter tech earnings season from a fundamental perspective, but elevated expectations may lead to company-specific volatility,” she said.

See also: US stock futures edge higher after chipmaker rally

“AI remains a long-term driver of earnings and economic growth, but investors are becoming more selective about which companies get rewarded from here,” said Anthony Saglimbene at Ameriprise. “For investors, that argues for owning AI exposure selectively rather than broadly, keeping technology concentration in check, and diversifying across market caps, sectors, and regions.”

Marking a sharp reversal from the broad-based rush into AI in recent years, investors are indeed becoming more selective and demanding with their bets on the technology. Elice Inc., a South Korean AI computing supplier scarcely known outside its home market, tanked 32% in its debut in Seoul.

While CoreWeave Inc. shares bounced, they have been under intense volatility as its bonds recently hit distressed levels on concerns over heavy borrowing.

“There are no signs that demand for AI is slowing,” said Angelo Kourkafas at Edward Jones. “We’re seeing healthy skepticism and a maturation of the theme, moving away from an environment where everything AI-related goes up toward a greater focus on quality and the companies with the deepest pockets to finance the investment needed to meet demand.”

Kourkafas noted that we’re also seeing earnings growth broaden beyond the largest companies. Against this backdrop, managing exposures is more important than trying to time pullbacks, he said.
